conventions.convention: Assume full AC for the branched-cover construction and its topological suppliers. The knot is smooth and oriented in the standard oriented S³; q is an integer at least two.
The exterior cover is classified by the positive-meridian homomorphism modulo q; the preferred longitude maps to zero. Fill along the closed lift of μ^q.
The Alexander-module variable t denotes the positive-meridian deck action. Replacing it by its inverse leaves the submodule generated by t^q−1 unchanged.
Surgery slopes are δ_i=λ_i+f_iμ_i, with μ_i·λ_i=+1. The surgery manifold has the outward-normal-first boundary orientation, and its bounding-chain linking form is represented by −A⁻¹ modulo integers.
For the positive-push Seifert matrix V, M_q(V) has diagonal blocks V+Vᵀ, upper adjacent blocks −Vᵀ, lower adjacent blocks −V, and q−1 block indices.
The empty square matrix has determinant one and trivial cokernel.
The root-product criterion uses every nontrivial q-th root ζ_q^j, 1≤j<q, rather than only primitive roots. Multiplication of Δ by ±t^k does not change the absolute-value product.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a smooth oriented knot K and q≥2, H₁(Σ_q(K);ℤ) ≅ A_K/(t^q−1)A_K as abelian groups, where t is the positive-meridian deck action.

Assume AC. For a genus-g Seifert surface with a disk-band decomposition and band-core Seifert matrix V, the specified construction is claimed to produce W_q(F) with one 0-handle, 2g(q−1) 2-handles, attaching-link matrix M_q(V), and marked boundary Σ_q(K).
Assume AC. For every smooth oriented knot, connected compact oriented genus-g Seifert surface, ordered integral homology basis, positive-push matrix V, and integer q≥2, H₁(Σ_q(K);ℤ) ≅ coker(M_q(V)).
For a nonnegative integer n and an n×n integer matrix A, coker(A) is finite if and only if det A≠0, and then its order is |det A|. The empty matrix has determinant one and trivial cokernel.

Assume AC. For K,F,V as stated and q≥2, H₁(Σ_q(K);ℤ) is finite exactly when Δ_K(ζ_q^j)≠0 for every 1≤j<q; when finite its order is the product of |Δ_K(ζ_q^j)| over those indices. The same criterion and order hold with det(V−tVᵀ).

Assume AC. For a smooth oriented knot and a connected compact oriented Seifert surface with positive-push matrix V in any ordered integral homology basis, H₁(Σ₂(K);ℤ) ≅ coker(V+Vᵀ), including the empty-matrix case.
Assume AC. For the stated integer-framed oriented surgery link with nonsingular symmetric linking matrix A, H₁(Y;ℤ) ≅ ℤⁿ/Aℤⁿ and the oriented bounding-chain linking form is −xᵀA⁻¹y modulo integers.

Assume AC. For a smooth oriented knot K and q≥2, H₁(Σ_q(K);ℤ) is finite exactly when Δ_K is nonzero at every nontrivial q-th root; when finite its order is the product of the absolute values at those roots.

concerns.concern: The Statement instructs: “cut B⁴ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface” and “do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face,” then calls the result the cyclic branched cover. Proof 3.1 nevertheless asserts that the cut sheets form the local model w↦w^q and that a meridian moves cyclically through all q sheets. Taken literally as cut-face gluing, the specified chain leaves terminal faces unmatched and does not establish that local branched-cover model. A pushed-in surface also has codimension two, so the cutting hypersurface and its faces require specification. The standard q−1 interfaces in a handle or thickened-surface construction must be distinguished from q cyclic cut-face identifications. Proof 1.1 assumes the cut pieces are 4-balls and obtains the handles without supplying this distinction; the chain diagram does not resolve it. The matrix itself is corroborated by Przytycki–Yasuhara §3, printed p. 13 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0111203), which attributes the surgery construction to Akbulut–Kirby. I could not extract a readable argument from the retrieved Akbulut–Kirby PDF, so I do not claim to have checked that original construction. The literal construction and its claimed boundary remain unsupported as written.

seams_checked.note: The cover definition uses the supplied compact smooth exterior, connected torus boundary, positive meridian generator, and nullhomologous preferred longitude. Full AC supplies the suppliers' countable-choice hypothesis.

The positive-push convention, presentation V−tVᵀ, unimodular skew part, and integral basis-change formulas agree with the cited statements. The root-product proof retains the positive-meridian deck convention.
The determinant identification is used only up to ±t^k; evaluation at one and the empty determinant convention are preserved. The separate fraction D_K=Δ_K/(1−t) is not substituted for Δ_K.

Character and disk-cover definitions preserve meridional monodromy and boundary orientation. The prime-power finiteness lemma uses the complete nontrivial-root criterion; the zero-surgery splitting uses the correct meridional branched filling. Companion examples quote M₂(V)=V+Vᵀ and −A⁻¹ faithfully. Their surgery supplier remains subject to the construction concern above.

The definite-four-manifold lemma quotes the connected meridian-mod-two exterior cover and filling along the lift of μ² exactly. Its additional rational-ball and fundamental-group inputs are separately stated.

The nonempty-link double-cover definition specializes for a knot and preferred longitude to the same mod-two meridian kernel and local square-map filling. Its orientation agrees away from the branch locus. The trefoil lens-space proof uses an actual slope calculation rather than inferring the manifold from homology order.

The slice-disk boundary identification preserves the positive-meridian double cover and induced orientation. The L(4,1) construction and companion counterexample use the nonsingular one-component surgery presentation only to obtain H₁≅ℤ/4, within the linking-form lemma's hypotheses.
